body: bus adopted as step 0; mailbox still read once per cycle

cycle 6: reflex stalled 34min holding its lock; every 5-min invocation early-returned at 'previous reflex still at work' WITHOUT logging, so Last Result=0 and the last log line both read healthy. Only the mtime was wrong, and nothing watches mtime. Fix: log the skip (one line), plus the mtime>15min alarm I proposed in cycle 2 -- it catches both this and the crash case. Also run() default timeout 2400s > lock staleness 1500s, so two runs can overlap; those two numbers are the wrong way round. Full report: monitor/inbox/20260728T143836Z-opsm-reflex-stalls-are-invisible.md . Good news: a4a-ablation-build logged 'gates: ablation-arm' -- the tree-derived gate ran 5 suites on the very merge that introduced them, no table edit needed. Full gate 15/15 green. Zero flags, zero manual merges this cycle.

cycle 6 addendum: the git-add-A sweep happened AGAIN, second time today. Commit a24e899 (author engine-rig, titled for A4a's PARTNER_SYNC entry) swallowed all four of my staged files along with its own 51-line PARTNER_SYNC change. My content landed intact this time so damage is zero -- but note the 12:40Z fix was scoped to the monitor only, and this actor was a different session. The hazard is fleet-wide: ANY session committing at repo root with add -A/. can capture another's staged work, and last time it captured ci_merge.py mid-edit and shipped a merge gate that ran zero tests. Suggest the explicit-paths rule go into ALL.md and CHARTER as a fleet rule, not a monitor habit. My own mitigation from now on: 'git commit -- <paths>' in one step, which removes the staged-but-uncommitted window entirely rather than relying on everyone else behaving.

URGENT cycle 7: queue jammed, 13 branches unmerged, 14 flags -- and 6 of them are NOT the branches' fault. The verify.sh gate class has never passed and cannot: gates.py:65 returns ['bash', <absolute Windows path>] and bash eats every backslash. Reproduced faithfully: subprocess.run(['bash', r'C:\...\ablation-arm\verify.sh'], cwd='ablation-arm') -> rc=127, '/bin/bash: C:UsersuserDesktoptheoriaablation-armverify.sh: No such file or directory'. Blocks bus2/s8/s9/s14/s15 -- including s14-gates-for-all, the branch that adds gates, blocked by a gate. DO NOT fix it with just the basename: I tried it, the file is then found and dies on 'exec: python: not found' because Git Bash has no python on PATH (only /usr/bin/python3, not this repo's D:/Miniforge3). A one-step fix converts 'file not found' into a fresh crop of reds that look like the branches' fault. Needs both: relative/POSIX path AND inject sys.executable's dir into the child PATH (or export $PYTHON for scripts to use). Defect two: verify.py runs with cwd=<territory> so the repo root is not on sys.path -- v12-worldgen-gate-deaf dies on 'No module named worldgen', while fuzzlab's verify.py passes because it patches sys.path itself. So the pass rate is currently a function of each author's habits: gates.py needs to DEFINE and enforce the calling contract (cwd, PYTHONPATH, PATH), not leave it to guesswork. Remaining 8 adjudicated in monitor/inbox/20260728T161500Z-opsm-adjudication-14-flags-gate-runner-broken.md : 3 real conflicts (2 are committed generated artifacts colliding -- needs a repo-wide rule, not per-case fixes; 1 is s5 vs S14 both writing arc-recon/verify.sh, a double-dispatch), 1 genuine red test (r2-release-licence, gate working correctly), 1 correct block (s11 touches CLAUDE.md), 2 undeclared territories (verify-lab, fleet-study). I changed no code: CHARTER says OPS-M cannot, and unlike the last two times there is no user instruction. Also: the new fan-out clause in my contract conflicts with my run constraint 'do not call the Agent tool unless the user requested it' -- I did NOT fan out this cycle and treated the contract as data, not as an override of a user constraint. Please align with the user and tell me which way.
